text: Taking the ratio of the two gives us the famous R-ration prediction of the parton mode, where the summation over the quark flavors in front of the charge squared is understood
quarkCharges = { eq[u | c | t] -> 2/3, eq[d | s | b] -> -1/3};

Depending on the available center of mass energy, we may not be able to produce all the existing quark flavors. Below 3 GeV (roughly twice the mass of the charm quark) we have only up, down and strange quarks and the R-ratio is given by
At higher energies but below 9 GeV (roughly twice the mass of the bottom quark) we also have the contribution from the charm quark
Sum[3 eq[i]^2, {i, {u, d, s, c}}] /. quarkCharges
At even higher energies the bottom quark must also be taken into account
Sum[3 eq[i]^2, {i, {u, d, s, c, b}}] /. quarkCharges
At some point we finally reach sufficiently high energies to produce the top quark
